sources.citation: Klamer, Marian. 2002. Timor-Leste survey word lists (unpublished; Lakalei list collected 2002-05-13, desa Fahinehan near Alas, speaker Domingus Pinto), as published in Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer (eds.), LexiRumah 3.0.0 (CLDF), lect laka1255, 272 forms.
sources.note: No prose statement; it is a phonetic wordlist whose IPA transcriptions carry primary-stress marks on 97 of 272 forms. My tally of marked word-parts: disyllables final-stressed 43 (saˈbɑi, huˈʔɑn, bɑˈtar, maˈsiː, boˈʔur, uˈsar - mostly ending in VV, long V or closed syllable), disyllables penult-stressed 26 (ˈmatɑn, ˈlala, ˈlita, ˈrabut), trisyllables penult-stressed 13 (laˈlɛhɑn, haˈtɛsi, tɑˈrulu), stressed monosyllables 15; 148 polysyllabic parts unmarked. Pattern resembles the right-edge penult~final alternation described for sister-lect Idaté (Alcantara 2014) but is data, not a rule.
